VHDL 2008 Grammar and Static Semantic Test Plan

Document Version: V2.0 Date: 2026-09-04 Standard: IEEE Std 1076-2008 Compliance: IEEE 829 Test Plan

1. Introduction

1.1 Purpose

This document defines the complete test plan for validating VHDL 2008 grammar (syntax) and compile/elaboration-stage static semantic rules. The test suite ensures 100% coverage of all BNF productions defined in Annex C of IEEE Std 1076-2008 and comprehensive coverage of high-frequency static semantic constraints.

This document defines the complete test plan for validating VHDL 2008 grammar (the syntax layer) and the static semantic rules at the compile/elaboration stage. The test suite ensures 100% coverage of all BNF productions defined in Annex C of IEEE Std 1076-2008 and comprehensive coverage of high-frequency core static semantic constraints.

1.2 Scope

Included: - All 310 BNF productions from Annex C (Syntax Summary) - 139 core static semantic rules detectable at compile/elaboration time - 37 VHDL predefined attributes with per-attribute test suites - Both positive (compilable) and negative (error-triggering) test cases

Excluded: - PSL assertions (PSL_Clock_Declaration, PSL_Property_Declaration, PSL_Sequence_Declaration, PSL_PSL_Directive) - Fixed-point and floating-point packages (IEEE 1076-2008 package bodies) - VHPI (VHDL Procedural Interface) - VITAL (ASIC modeling extensions) - Vendor-specific language extensions - All runtime semantic behaviors: simulation timing, delta delays, execution order, event scheduling, signal resolution at runtime

1.3 Test Objectives

  1. Verify that each BNF production is correctly recognized by a VHDL 2008-compliant parser
  2. Verify that single violations of BNF productions are correctly detected
  3. Verify that static semantic constraints are enforced at compile/elaboration
  4. Provide full traceability from test cases back to standard clauses

2. Test Strategy

2.1 Test Case Design Methodology

Syntax Testing

Aspect Positive (SYN, QSYN) Negative (SNN, QSNN)
Count per BNF rule 3-5 (basic) + 4 (quality) 2-3 (basic) + 3 (quality)
Design Complete VHDL unit with complex custom types (integer/enum/array/record subtypes) Syntactically invalid but only one rule violated
Expected result Compiles successfully Triggers specific syntax error

Semantic Testing

Aspect Positive (SEM) Negative (SMN)
Count per semantic rule 1 2
Design Syntactically valid, semantically correct Syntactically valid, semantically invalid (single rule violation)
Expected result Compiles and elaborates successfully Triggers specific semantic error

2.2 Single-Rule Per Negative Case Constraint

Every negative test case must violate exactly ONE rule. This ensures error messages can be uniquely attributed to a specific rule.

Every negative test case must violate exactly one rule, and no more. This ensures that error messages can be uniquely traced back to a specific rule.

2.3 Test Case Naming Convention

New chapter-based format:

TC_[PRODUCTION_NAME]_[TYPE]_[NNN].vhd


    

  • PRODUCTION_NAME: BNF production name, uppercase (e.g., ARCHITECTURE_BODY, ENTITY_DECLARATION)
    • 

  • TYPE: SYN (syntax positive), SNN (syntax negative), QSYN (quality positive), QSNN (quality negative), SEM (semantic positive), SMN (semantic negative)
    • 

  • Example: TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_001.vhd, TC_ENTITY_DECLARATION_QSYN_001.vhd
    • 



Legacy format (syntax/semantic/attributes directories):


TC_[MODULE]_[TYPE]_[NNN].vhd


    

  • MODULE: 3-letter abbreviation (DU, LEX, TYPE, DECL, SUBP, ENT, SEQ, CONC, CFG)
    • 

  • Example: TC_TYPE_SYN_001.vhd, TC_DECL_SMN_001.vhd
    • 





3. Test Suite Architecture


3.1 Primary Organization: IEEE Chapter Structure


The test suite is organized by IEEE 1076-2008 chapter, with each BNF production as a subfolder.

├── ch04_subprograms_packages/  21f, 319 files,  SYN=195 SNN=79 SEM=0 SMN=16 (specific=21)

├── ch09_expressions/  32f, 557 files,  SYN=275 SNN=168 SEM=35 SMN=57 (specific=16)
├── ch10_sequential/  55f, 823 files,  SYN=362 SNN=241 SEM=28 SMN=146 (specific=28)
├── ch11_concurrent/  23f, 364 files,  SYN=137 SNN=105 SEM=31 SMN=62 (specific=22)

├── ch15_lexical/  22f, 342 files,  SYN=120 SNN=108 SEM=0 SMN=88 (specific=22)
│
│   Each folder: SYN + SNN + SEM + SMN (generic + production-specific)
└── Grand total: 5,185 files, 328 production folders


3.2 Per-Production Folder Structure


Each production folder contains all test types colocated: - SYN files (3-5): basic positive tests with rich type declarations - QSYN files (4): quality positive tests — comprehensive with all type categories - SNN files (2-3): basic negative tests — production-specific syntax errors - QSNN files (3): quality negative tests — single-rule violation - SEM files (1-3): semantic positive tests — respects the semantic constraint - SMN files (2-3): semantic negative tests — violates exactly one semantic rule

4. Test Environment


4.1 Tools

    •

4.2 Test Data


All test cases are self-contained VHDL design files. No external data files, simulation models, or vendor libraries required. Each file is a complete compilable unit (entity + architecture or package declaration + body).


All test cases are self-contained VHDL design files, requiring no external dependencies.

9.1 architecture_body (Ch.3, Design Entities)


Category: Category A (standalone compilation units) | Total files: 46


SYN — Positive syntax tests (23 files)










File
How to Test






TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_001.vhd
minimal: empty declarative, single assignment




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_002.vhd
types: custom integer/enum/array/record, subtypes, constants, aliases




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_003.vhd
Subprogram declarations and bodies in the declarative part: pure function + impure function + procedure declaration + procedure body, actually calling them in concurrent statements, verifying subprograms can be declared and defined in architecture_declarative_part




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_004.vhd
Multiple processes coexisting: clock process (clk sensitivity) + reset process (rst_n sensitivity) + combinational process (a,b sensitivity) + wait-based process, verifying architecture_statement_part can contain any number of process concurrent statements in any style




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_005.vhd
generates: for-generate, if-generate-else, nested generate, component inst with generic+port map




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_006.vhd
blocks: simple block, guarded block, nested blocks




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_007.vhd
same entity dual architectures: structural vs behavioral style




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_008.vhd
concurrent: postponed assertion, immediate assertion, concurrent signal assignment




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_009.vhd
VHDL 2008: protected type, shared variable, subprogram in architecture, all declarations




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_010.vhd
comprehensive: all declarative items + all concurrent statements combined




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_011.vhd
Unconstrained port + generic combination: entity uses an unconstrained array port and a generic to control size, the declarative part derives the index range from the generic value, for-generate iterates the generic parameter, verifying full architecture support for generics and unconstrained ports




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_012.vhd
Multi-level configuration binding: architecture declarative part contains component declaration + configuration specification (for…use entity…port map) and instantiates that component, verifying architecture_declarative_part can contain a configuration specification whose binding takes effect at architecture instantiation




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_013.vhd
Guarded signal disconnect specification: declarative part contains a disconnect specification defining post-disconnection behavior for a guarded signal, a guarded block uses guarded assignment to that signal, verifying architecture_declarative_part can contain disconnect_specification and interact correctly with the guarded block




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_014.vhd
Group declarations: declarative part contains a group_template_declaration (defining the allowed entity class combinations) and a group_declaration (using that template to group signals into a named group), verifying architecture_declarative_part supports the complete group construct (VHDL 2008 group feature)




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_015.vhd
VHDL 2008 external names: an architecture process uses the <<signal external pathname : type>> syntax to reference a hierarchical external signal, verifying the statement part of the architecture can use external_name for cross-level signal access (VHDL 2008 hierarchical reference)




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_016.vhd
Minimal end form: empty declarative part + empty statement part, after end neither the “architecture” keyword nor the architecture name identifier is written, just end; — verifying both optional clauses [ architecture ] [ architecture_simple_name ] in the BNF can be omitted at the same time




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_017.vhd
Architecture containing only passive concurrent procedure calls: statement part consists of 2 concurrent_procedure_call_statements (both passive procedures, driving no signals), verifying entity_statement and architecture_statement_part allow passive concurrent procedure calls as the only concurrent statement form




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_018.vhd
All block header combinations: 4 blocks use (no header), (generic only), (port only), and (generic+port combined) respectively, verifying all 4 combinations of the block_statement block_header compile in the architecture statement part




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_019.vhd
Large-scale multi-component instantiation: declarative part declares 2 component kinds (flip-flop + inverter), for-generate batch-instantiates 8 flip-flops + 8 inverters forming a shift chain, verifying the architecture can contain many component_instantiations and for-generate can iterate multiple components




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_020.vhd
File declarations and operations: declarative part contains a file type definition (file of integer) and a file object declaration (with open_read_mode/file_logical_name), the statement part uses the file type through a subprogram, verifying architecture_declarative_part supports file_declaration and file_type_definition




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_021.vhd
Access types and allocators: declarative part contains an access type (pointer to a record) and an allocator (new expression), a process uses the access object to store and read data, verifying architecture_declarative_part supports access_type_definition and allocator expressions




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_022.vhd
All alias categories: declarative part contains an object alias (signal alias with subtype_indication), a subprogram alias (function alias with signature), and an enumeration literal alias, the statement part drives the same signal through the original name and the alias, verifying all three forms of alias_declaration are legal in architecture_declarative_part




TC_ARCHITECTURE_BODY_SYN_023.vhd
Mixed VHDL 2008 features: declarative part contains protected type declaration + body + shared variable and an impure function, statement part contains a matching case? statement (VHDL 2008), verifying the architecture can mix multiple VHDL 2008 new syntax elements (protected type, shared var, case? matching statement)

Rule

How to Test






SEM_ARCH_001
TC_SEM_ARCH_001_SEM_001.vhd

TC_SEM_ARCH_001_SMN_001.vhd

TC_SEM_ARCH_001_SMN_002.vhd

TC_SEM_ARCH_002_SEM_002.vhd

SEM_ARCH_002
TC_SEM_ARCH_002_SMN_003.vhd

SEM_ARCH_002
TC_SEM_ARCH_002_SMN_004.vhd

SEM_ARCH_003

SEM_ARCH_004
TC_SEM_ARCH_004_SEM_004.vhd
Positive case: architecture contains 3 generate statements (for-generate “gen_ff”, if-generate “gen_inv”, for-generate “gen_out”), each with a different label name, verifying differently named generate labels can coexist with component inst/concurrent assignment/block inside




SEM_ARCH_004
TC_SEM_ARCH_004_SMN_006.vhd
Negative case: 2 for-generates both use label “gen_same”, the second generate finds a label conflict in the architecture statement part, verifying the analyzer applies the same declarative-region uniqueness check to generate_label as to signals/constants

9.99 component_declaration (Ch.6, Declarations)

SYN — Positive syntax tests (11 files)










File
How to Test






TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SYN_001.vhd
Component full form: with generic_clause(2 generics integer+time) + port_clause(4 ports all modes) / end component with identifier, verifying the complete generic+port form of component_declaration




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SYN_002.vhd
Minimal component_declaration — only mandatory tokens: ‘component’, identifier, ‘end component’. No optional ‘is’, no generic_clause, no port_clause, no component_simple_name after end component. Exercises the shortest grammatically valid form of the production.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SYN_003.vhd
Component with the optional ‘is’ keyword present, no generic_clause, no port_clause, and no component_simple_name after ‘end component’. Verifies the parser correctly handles ‘is’ as an isolated optional token within the production.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SYN_004.vhd
Component with generic_clause only (no port_clause). Generics of mixed types — integer with default and time with default. Exercises comma-separated generic list syntax within the component body. End component without simple_name.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SYN_005.vhd
Component with port_clause only (no generic_clause). Exercises four port modes — in, out, inout, buffer — with bit and bit_vector types. Uses multi-line port layout. No generic_clause, end component without simple_name.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SYN_006.vhd
Complete component_declaration with all optional elements: ‘is’ keyword, generic_clause with integer and time defaults, port_clause with in/out/inout modes using generic-dependent bit_vector widths, and end component with matching component_simple_name. Exercises the full BNF production.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SYN_007.vhd
Component declaration using IEEE std_logic/std_logic_vector port types with in/out modes. Exercises component_declaration with standard logic types — a common real-world hardware design pattern for register-file components. Uses library ieee clause for std_logic visibility.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SYN_008.vhd
Component exercising all five port modes — in, out, inout, buffer, linkage — in a single port_clause. No generic_clause. Tests that the parser accepts every mode keyword in the component port context. End component without simple_name.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SYN_009.vhd
Multiple component declarations in a single architecture declarative part. Four distinct declarations exercise different combinations of optional clauses: minimal (bare), generic-only, port-only, and full generic+port with end component simple_name. Verifies the parser handles consecutive component_declarations without interference.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SYN_010.vhd
Component with generic_clause only (no port_clause) and end component includes the component_simple_name. No ‘is’ keyword. Exercises the generic+end-identifier combination without ports, verifying all three tokens of the end clause.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SYN_011.vhd
Component with boolean and bit_vector generic types plus port_clause. Exercises generic types beyond integer/time — boolean with default TRUE, and bit_vector with aggregate default. Includes ‘is’ keyword and end component without simple_name. Verifies the parser handles non-numeric generic types correctly.






SNN — Negative syntax tests (8 files)










File
How to Test






TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SNN_001.vhd
Syntactically invalid component_declaration — missing the mandatory ‘component’ keyword. The declaration begins directly with an identifier where the parser expects ‘component’. File is parseable up to the unexpected ‘comp_bad’ identifier.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SNN_002.vhd
Syntactically invalid component_declaration — the terminating ‘end component’ clause is entirely missing. The declaration opens correctly with ‘component’ and a valid port_clause, but no ‘end component;’ is provided. Error triggered when the next construct (signal declaration or ‘begin’) is encountered where ‘end component’ was expected. File is parseable through the valid port_clause.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SNN_003.vhd
SNN: port_clause of component_declaration missing the closing parenthesis - in component comp_nomode the port list has end component directly after the interface declaration without ‘)’, verifying the interface list of port_clause requires a closing parenthesis




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SNN_004.vhd
Syntactically invalid component_declaration — generic_clause uses comma as separator between generic declarations. VHDL generic and port interface lists require semicolons as element separators, not commas. Error at the comma after the first generic element.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SNN_005.vhd
Syntactically invalid component_declaration — port_clause uses comma as separator between port elements. Like generic_clause, the port list requires semicolons between interface element declarations. Error at the comma after the first port element.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SNN_006.vhd
Syntactically invalid component_declaration — missing semicolon after ‘end component’. The production requires a terminating semicolon after the closing clause. Error at the next token (‘begin’) where ‘;’ is expected. File is parseable through the complete component body up to the missing semicolon.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SNN_007.vhd
Syntactically invalid component_declaration — the terminating clause has ‘end’ but is missing the required ‘component’ keyword. The production mandates ‘end component’ as a compound keyword pair. Error at the semicolon where ‘component’ was expected after ‘end’.




TC_COMPONENT_DECLARATION_SNN_008.vhd
Syntactically invalid component_declaration — port element missing the type specification. A port ‘clk’ has mode ‘in’ but no type/subtype_indication follows. The interface_element production requires both mode and type. Error at the closing parenthesis or next element where a type was expected.
